subject.title: [security] SSH connections inherit local agent forwarding despite per-lease key scoping

question: Should Crabbox unconditionally disable inherited OpenSSH agent/X11 forwarding on all SSH-backed transports, or provide a trusted operator opt-in for workflows that intentionally need it?
rationale: The source-level gap is reproducible, but the remediation changes a security boundary and may affect existing SSH-config workflows, so maintainer intent is needed before automation changes defaults or adds configuration surface.

options.title: Default deny with trusted opt-in
options.body: Add forwarding-deny options everywhere by default and allow re-enabling only through explicit trusted user config or CLI surface with warning/docs.

options.title: Default deny only
options.body: Add forwarding-deny options everywhere and do not support agent or X11 forwarding through Crabbox-managed SSH transports.

options.title: Document as hardening for now
options.body: Leave current inheritance behavior in place temporarily and document the risk, accepting that per-lease SSH guidance remains incomplete.

recommendation.title: Default deny with trusted opt-in
recommendation.body: Add forwarding-deny options everywhere by default and allow re-enabling only through explicit trusted user config or CLI surface with warning/docs.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant SSH transport history and prior security-boundary decisions are most clearly tied to this person.
